upstream.scope: Server-authoritative column chooser for the process table over the existing cheap catalogued columns (PID, Name, Resident, CPU): show, hide, reorder and restore defaults through standard native Buttons and standard ACTIVATE events; the table's columns property and every row's cells are republished in the chosen sequence by SET_PROPERTY and MODEL_UPDATE, never by recreating the table, its model or any row; no process action, no expensive collector, no protocol or client change

entries.feature: A column layout is a non-empty sequence of distinct catalogued process columns owned by the server (ColumnLayout); the default preset is the catalogued PROCESS_LIST; a layout naming no column or one column twice is refused and commits nothing; the last visible column cannot be hidden

Rows keep every catalogued cell and typed sort value server-side and publish only the visible columns in layout order; a layout change sets the table's columns and updates each changed row in place under its own ItemId, so no committed revision lacks a row a client had selected, the active sort is kept even when its column is hidden, and later refreshes publish in the chosen layout
entries.scope: PX-068/projection (src/projection.rs) and refresh (src/refresh.rs) ProcessView::set_columns, restore_default_columns, click_column

entries.feature: The chooser is a row of standard Buttons — hide/show, move left and move right per column, and restore default columns — whose labels state what a click does and which are disabled when a click could change nothing; each ACTIVATE is applied before it is acknowledged, a replayed click is answered from its settled result, and the PX-008 audit admits exactly these node constants with ACTIVATE
